_about.one_line: Our equation library: 67 concepts as dependency-free Rust, with their definitions, laws and recorded spec rows; free for the community.
_about.source: emit/*.rs, emit/index.json, specs/specs.jsonl, laws/mathkb.json; every row re-run on 2026-10-16 on an Intel i5-8365U laptop (rustc 1.98.0), logs in results/

tests.title: 39 emitted equations reproduce their 3,245 recorded spec rows
tests.claim: Compiled with rustc from this repository alone, 39 emitted concept files give the recorded output on every row of their spec (3,245 rows): 39 passed, 0 failed
tests.verify: python3 -I tools/verify.py . | tail -1 | grep -q '"pass": true' && echo ok
tests.what_it_means: Each emitted file is one equation turned into a small Rust program. The spec file holds rows of inputs and the output the definition gives. This test compiles each program into a temporary folder and runs it on its rows; the program stops with an error if any answer differs. Passing means the shipped Rust really computes the specified function on all recorded rows.
tests.how_we_got_it: tools/verify.py reads emit/index.json and specs/specs.jsonl, rustc -C opt-level=1 each emit/<concept>.rs, writes the rows (the way the development tree's status.py does) and runs the binary. 2026-10-16, Intel i5-8365U laptop, rustc 1.98.0: 39 passed, 0 failed, 3,245 rows (results/2026-10-16-verify.log; about 11 s).
tests.use_in_your_work: Drop a concept file into your own project (gcd, modexp, NTT, Montgomery product) and keep its rows as test vectors.
tests.honest_limits: Rows are those recorded when the equation was built; they are not an exhaustive test. 28 of the 67 concepts have no rows here (Q5).

tests.title: Negative control: tampered rows make every program fail
tests.claim: With every recorded output changed on purpose, all 39 programs reject their rows (39/39), so Q1's pass is not vacuous
tests.verify: python3 -I tools/verify.py . --teeth | tail -1 | grep -q '"pass": true' && echo ok
tests.what_it_means: Same compile-and-run as Q1 but with wrong expected outputs. Each program has to fail. Passing means the row check can fail.
tests.use_in_your_work: Use the same tamper test on your own harness.
tests.honest_limits: Shows the check can fail; says nothing more about the equations.

tests.title: The 39 concept laws hold on fresh draws
tests.claim: The laws in laws/mathkb.json, one per spec'd concept, hold on 300 fresh seeded draws each: 39 laws, 0 failures
tests.verify: python3 -I tools/lawcheck.py . | tail -1 | grep -q '"pass": true' && echo ok
tests.what_it_means: Properties (not definitions) that each concept must satisfy, with generators of random inputs, are re-run in plain Python. Passing means they all hold on new draws.
tests.how_we_got_it: tools/lawcheck.py, 2026-10-16, laptop: 39 laws x 300 draws, 0 failed (results/2026-10-16-lawcheck.log).
tests.use_in_your_work: Property-test your own port of any of these equations.
tests.honest_limits: Random draws only; the laws test the concepts, which are the same functions as the Rust files only through the shared spec rows (Q1).

tests.title: Every emitted file compiles and the index matches the files
tests.claim: All 67 emitted Rust files compile; emit/index.json and emit/*.rs name the same 67 concepts; every recorded equation has balanced parentheses
tests.verify: python3 -I tools/verify.py . --compile | tail -1 | grep -q '"pass": true' && echo ok
tests.what_it_means: The structural check: nothing in the library is a broken or orphaned file, including the 28 concepts that have no rows here.
tests.use_in_your_work: Confidence that a concept file builds on a stock Rust toolchain with no dependencies.
tests.honest_limits: Compiling is not correctness; correctness is Q1 for the 39 and the build receipts for the rest.

tests.title: Honest negative: 28 concepts cannot be re-verified from this repository
tests.claim: 28 of 67 concepts (the codec, range-decoder, ring-arithmetic and shuffle ones) have no spec rows here; the verifier lists them as NOT-RE-VERIFIABLE-HERE instead of counting them
tests.verify: python3 -c 'import json,subprocess; r=subprocess.run(['"'"'python3'"'"','"'"'-I'"'"','"'"'tools/verify.py'"'"','"'"'.'"'"','"'"'--only'"'"','"'"'idct4,vp9_lf4,ring_ln,rd_step'"'"'],capture_output=True,text=True); lines=[x for x in r.stdout.splitlines() if '"'"'NOT-RE-VERIFIABLE-HERE'"'"' in x]; names={x.split('"'"':'"'"',1)[0] for x in lines}; d=json.loads(r.stdout.splitlines()[-1]); assert r.returncode==1 and names=={'"'"'idct4'"'"','"'"'vp9_lf4'"'"','"'"'ring_ln'"'"','"'"'rd_step'"'"'} and len(lines)==4 and d['"'"'passed'"'"']==0 and d['"'"'failed'"'"']==0 and d['"'"'not_reverifiable'"'"']==4 and d['"'"'pass'"'"'] is False; print(4)'
tests.what_it_means: Those 28 concepts were checked at build time against a black-box reference (rows checked per concept are in the receipts) but their rows and references are not part of this repository, and none of them has a cemented law yet. The verifier says so rather than passing them.
tests.how_we_got_it: tools/verify.py --only <four of the 28>, 2026-10-16: 4 listed, 0 passed (results/2026-10-16-not-reverifiable.log). The build receipts: results/2026-10-16-factory-receipts.json (45 concepts incl. these).
tests.use_in_your_work: Treat these 28 as emitted but unconfirmed by you until you check them against the published specification they cite.
tests.honest_limits: Receipts are recorded results, not re-run here.
corrections: E2 2026-10-17: explicitly assert the verifier intentional exit1 and exactly four unavailable concepts; preserve negative under pipefail.
